known_facts_book1: Crooked little sprites who come to Ozma's party from the great Forest of Burzee, brought by Santa Claus.
Have long whiskers, pointed caps, and curling toes, and are no taller than Button-Bright's shoulder.
Their duty is to water and care for the young trees of the forest, which hard work makes them crooked and gnarled like the trees.
Dance the Fairy Circle at the banquet and float home in small bubbles with Santa Claus.

known_relations_book1.Santa Claus: Their beloved master, who brings them to Oz to see the city.
known_relations_book1.Ryls: Their fellow sprites who also come with Santa Claus.

known_facts_book1: The people of the yellow western Country of Oz, ruled by the Tin Woodman as their Emperor.
Their color is yellow and almost everything in their country that has any color is yellow.
Are the cleverest tinsmiths in the world and built the Tin Woodman's tin castle.
Once were made slaves by a wicked witch until Dorothy melted her; then they made Nick Chopper their Emperor.
Provide a tin orchestra at the castle and a Tin Band that plays 'There's No Plate like Tin' in the procession.

known_relations_book1.Tin Woodman: Their Emperor, Nick Chopper, whom they love dearly.
known_relations_book1.Dorothy: The girl who freed them by melting the wicked witch.

known_facts_book1: A vast waste of grey sand that surrounds the Land of Oz and turns any living flesh that touches it to dust in an instant.
A large white warning sign at its edge forbids anyone to venture upon it.
Is crossed by the party in Johnny Dooit's wind-driven sand-boat, whose runners keep them off the sand.
The sand-boat smashes on the rocks at the Oz side of the desert, but everyone lands safely on the grass.

known_relations_book1.Johnny Dooit: Builds the sand-boat that lets the party cross the desert.
known_relations_book1.Dorothy: Has crossed it before by cyclone, Silver Shoes, Magic Carpet, and Magic Belt.

known_facts_book1: The magnificent capital in the center of Oz, where the corners of the four countries meet, ruled by Princess Ozma.
Its buildings are plated with gold and set with emeralds, and it is entered through jeweled gates kept by the Guardian of the Gates.
Ozma's birthday celebration is held on the broad green just outside its gates.
At the end the Love Magnet is hung over its gates so that whoever enters or leaves may be loved and loving.

known_relations_book1.Ozma: Its ruler, who holds her birthday celebration there.
known_relations_book1.Love Magnet: Hung over the city gates at the story's close.
known_relations_book1.Guardian of the Gates: The little green-spectacled man who opens the gates.

known_facts_book1: Dorothy's home, on Uncle Henry and Aunt Em's farm, where the book opens.
Called by Dorothy 'the unromantic State of Kansas', where she gets lost within fifteen minutes near her own farm-house.
Butterfield, the town the shaggy man is avoiding, lies near Dorothy's farm.
Dorothy notes that magic will not work in Kansas, only in fairy countries.

known_relations_book1.Dorothy: Her home state, to which she is returned by the Magic Belt at the end.

known_facts_book1: Ozma's palace in the Emerald City, set in walled green-marble gardens, where the guests are lodged and the banquet is held.
Contains Ozma's malachite throne, the great Throne-Room where guests are received, and Dorothy's own suite of rooms.
The shaggy man is given one of its handsomest apartments, with a marble bath and a chest of jeweled ornaments.
Tik-tok lives at the palace, and the Tin Woodman always has the same room there when he visits.

known_relations_book1.Ozma: The Ruler whose palace it is.
known_relations_book1.Jellia Jamb: Ozma's attendant who welcomes guests at its door.
